I’ll verify the supplied scan against the fixture’s test and source files, then separate assertion-backed behavior from tests that merely execute code.

The global `crimes` binary isn’t installed in this environment. I’ll use the repository’s locally built CLI if present; the supplied JSON remains the scan contract I’m validating.

The refactor safety is uneven: rates and parts of invoice construction have assertion-backed tests; reporting and ledger mostly have execution coverage that can stay green while behavior is wrong.

| Area | Actual protection |
|---|---|
| [`billing/rates.py`](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/12-py-tested/billing/rates.py>) | Genuinely assertion-backed. [`test_rates.py`](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/12-py-tested/tests/test_rates.py>) verifies GB/DE rates, the unknown-region fallback, and non-zero-rated behavior for GB/FR. |
| [`billing/invoices.py`](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/12-py-tested/billing/invoices.py>) | Assertion-backed through imported helpers and a base class in [`tests/support.py`](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/12-py-tested/tests/support.py>). The suite checks invoice balance, non-negative net, selected gross totals, and account preservation. This is why `crimes` correctly did **not** flag [`test_invoices.py`](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/12-py-tested/tests/test_invoices.py>) merely because assertions are outside the test bodies. |
| `apply_credit` | Only partly protected. Tests named “reduces the total” and “zero credit is a no-op” merely check that the resulting invoice remains balanced and non-negative. They never compare old and new totals or prove that zero credit preserves the invoice. The names promise more than the assertions enforce. |
| [`billing/reporting.py`](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/12-py-tested/billing/reporting.py>) | Only looks covered. All four tests in [`test_reporting.py`](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/12-py-tested/tests/test_reporting.py:11>) have zero assertions. Incorrect report fields, totals, CSV, or JSON can pass as long as no exception is raised. The “round trip” test also checks no round-trip result. Unsupported-format behavior is untested. |
| [`billing/ledger.py`](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/12-py-tested/billing/ledger.py>) | No dedicated tests. `post_entry` is executed indirectly by the hollow reporting tests, so line coverage may make it appear protected, but its result is not validated. `reverse_entry` is not exercised. |

The scan produced one high-confidence, high-severity `weak_test_signal`: 4/4 reporting tests contain no assertion. Also, the JSON `coverage` block means **scanner file-discovery coverage**, not test coverage. Its “9 Python files” does not mean all nine are behaviorally tested, and the existing `.coverage` file was not read by the scan.
